card.name: Prepositions before US place names
card.fires_on: Small linking words (at, across, the, to, near) right before a proper place or company name, mostly in North Carolina and Southern US local history or news text.

modes.label: Preposition before a place
modes.description: A preposition or 'the' sits just before a named gap, town, river or mill.
modes.example: seven hand-dug tunnels<< across>> the Swannanoa Gap, costing

modes.label: Direction word in rail or travel
modes.description: A verb or 'to' leading toward a destination town on a railroad route.
modes.example: opened 84 miles of track from Salisbury<< to>> Morganton.

card.writes: It nudges the model toward proper names of places, such as Beam, Holland, Western and Hague, rather than ones like African or Virgin.
card.plain: It fires on small words like 'at' or 'to' when a specific place name is about to come next.
